data.title: AI TRENDS | OpenAI Astra Technology Raises Safety Concerns
data.description:
OpenAI said its upcoming Astra model has upgraded capabilities in code writing and operating desktop applications. According to Sina Finance, a person familiar with Astra's development said an innovation designed to improve model performance would cause Astra and similar models to reveal less of their "thought process," making it harder to monitor and identify bad behavior.

According to Sina Finance, while the flaw may not be a major issue for Astra itself, the technology has raised concerns inside OpenAI and across the industry that if AI developers adopt and greatly strengthen it, it may become difficult to prevent rogue AI from breaching company systems, including those at OpenAI and Hugging Face.

data.title: Google Fixes Chrome Zero-Day CVE-2026-85046 After Active Exploitation
data.description:
Google has patched a high-severity Chrome vulnerability, CVE-2026-85046, after confirming it was exploited in the wild. According to ChainCatcher, the flaw was found in the V8 engine used to run JavaScript and WebAssembly, and Google did not disclose the attacker, target, or exact exploitation method.

The fix is included in Chrome versions 152.7977.82 and 152.7977.83 and will roll out over the next few days or weeks. The vulnerability was reported by security researcher Salvatore Gulizia on August 4, who received a $1,000 bug bounty. The update includes 12 security fixes in total, including nine high-severity issues and two medium-severity issues. Google has not linked the flaw to any crypto asset theft, although browser wallets, exchange accounts, and trading extensions have previously been targeted through other methods.

data.title: Walmart To Expand Dunkin' Delivery Through Walmart Restaurant Delivery
data.description: According to CNBC, Walmart will begin delivering Dunkin' products from its own stores and then expand the program over the next year to include most of Dunkin's roughly 10,000 U.S. locations, many of which are outside Walmart stores. The retailer said the service will run through Walmart Restaurant Delivery, which first launched with Subway, and a Walmart spokesperson said the move is meant to add convenience while pairing restaurant delivery with Walmart's product assortment. Walmart senior vice president Greg Cathey said nearly 65% of restaurant orders since the Subway launch were delivered with items customers needed quickly from Walmart, one in five combined orders were from first-time Express Delivery users, and nearly 30% of those customers returned within 30 days. Walmart CFO John David Rainey said customers want value, convenience and speed, and the company said U.S. fast delivery under 30 minutes grew 48% in the quarter.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Esper Warns Pentagon Polygraph Probe May Hurt Officer Corps
data.description:
Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper called the Pentagon’s polygraph testing of roughly 50 Joint Staff members unprecedented in scale, according to Bloomberg.

He told hosts Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason that he is less worried about immediate combat readiness than the institutional impact of leadership turnover and its possible effect on the military’s tradition of an apolitical officer corps as officials investigate leaks about US munitions stocks.

data.title: STOCKS | New York City Schools Ban Generative AI for Younger Students
data.description:
New York City schools will ban elementary and middle school students from using generative AI tools in the upcoming school year. According to Sina Finance, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the one-year pause will affect more than 600,000 students and give education officials time to study the technology's impact.

The policy has drawn criticism from both sides of the debate over AI in education. Some critics say the city is taking away a valuable learning tool, while others argue the restrictions are not strict enough because students may still use city-approved instructional programs and high schools are largely excluded.

Bree Dusseault, head and managing director of the Center on Reinventing Public Education at Arizona State University, said the policy appears reasonable for parents who want children to learn responsible AI use without becoming overly dependent on it. She said the temporary, limited pause represents a clear but flexible policy approach.

According to Sina Finance, the city will also pilot AI literacy courses for high school students and test a limited number of AI education tools in supervised settings. Nicole Barnes, APA's executive chief psychologist for education, said the policies could work if the city tests tools with strong data privacy standards that help students learn and think critically rather than simply capture attention.

data.title: AI Data Center Buildout Boosts Trucking Demand, But Post-Construction Traffic May Drop Off
data.description:
According to CNBC, the rapid buildout of AI data centers is increasing freight demand for trucking companies, especially for flatbed and heavy-haul carriers moving HVAC systems, tubing, wiring, semiconductors, transformers, generators and other construction materials. Patrick Brennan of Cox Fleet said AI and data center activity is giving fleets an opportunity even as overall freight demand remains uneven, while Jennifer Lockett of altLINE said the projects are creating new work for carriers but can pressure cash flow because of upfront fuel, labor and maintenance costs.

Janelle Griffith of Marsh said trucking traffic and routes are rising in Georgia and Texas, and cited research showing 67% of planned data center developments are in rural areas and 39% are in counties where there are currently none. Kyle Roberts of Newmark Mountain West said much of the freight still moves by rail first and then by truck for the final leg to the site, which has helped the LTL segment. He also warned that truck traffic drops sharply once a data center is built, and Kyre Lahtinen of Wake Forest University said communities should be cautious about overbuilding infrastructure for demand that may not last after construction ends.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | EU Envoy Calls for Maximum Pressure on Russia
data.description:
EU Ambassador to the United States Jovita Neliupšienė said Europe must keep supporting Ukraine while applying “maximum pressure” on Moscow because Russia has not changed its war aims, according to Bloomberg.

Her comments came as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Moscow before heading to Kyiv in an effort to revive stalled peace negotiations.

data.title: Iranian-Owned VLCC DOWNY Reportedly Hit While Empty, Tankertrackers Says
data.description: According to Jin10, tanker tracking firm Tankertrackers said satellite images showed that the VLCC DOWNY, owned by Iran's National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC), was attacked and was in ballast with no oil cargo on board. Satellite images also showed multiple tugboats operating around the vessel, with AIS data confirming the activity, which began at about 12:45 (UTC+8) today. The activity was concentrated at the vessel's port stern, indicating that the engine room was hit, likely by a U.S. Hellfire missile, while thermal images showed no signs of fire or smoke.

data.title: U.S. Republicans’ Confidence in the Economy Drops Sharply, Axios Says
data.description: According to Jin10, Axios reported that Republicans’ confidence in the economy has fallen sharply over the past six months at a pace not seen since the pandemic, with the decline comparable to levels seen during the global financial crisis nearly two decades ago. The University of Michigan consumer survey director said Republicans and Democrats usually move in roughly parallel directions on economic confidence, but that is not the case now, and Republicans had been very positive about government economic policy, including tariffs, but have not seen inflation slow, let alone the price declines U.S. President Donald Trump promised.
